newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, seen guarded.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, seen guarded.

text.p: Argentine stocks posted new strong gains Monday but traders warned the outlook had turned volatile ahead of key U.S. economic data this week.
"The market is basically firm, but I advise a lot of caution because prices have reached very decent levels and volume is starting to shrink," said Leonardo Torres Barsanti at analysts Rio Research.

The weighted MerVal index posted its fifth running gain, rising 1.3 percent to 852.20. It stands 7.8 higher since last Monday's close and has recovered most losses incurred earlier this month on devaluation fears in Brazil.
"Unless company results come in much stronger than expected, the MerVal has already reached its year-end target so there will be fewer short-term positions," Barsanti said.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Monday its 12-month target for the MerVal was 1,000, representing gains of nearly 20 percent -- provided U.S. long bond yields stay at 6.5 percent, earnings per share show real growth of 14 percent and spreads of domestic bonds over U.S. treasuries remain stable.
Floor volume eased to 30.6 million pesos in the session from 36.8 million Friday, while over-the-counter turnover slowed to 102.6 million pesos from 116.5 million Friday.
The broad market index closed up 0.7 percent, with winners smashing losers 37 to 13 and 23 issues closing flat.

Top main-tier gainers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, carmaker Ciadea and utility Central Costanera, which surged 10 percent, 7.5 percent and 4.4 percent, respectively. Celulosa's rise was not seen as significant "because it's a very erratic stock and it traded with scant volume," a trader said.
Strongest MerVal losers were steelmaker Siderca, foods giant Molinos Rio de la Plata and Banco Frances, which shed 2.2 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
